_comment: Accepted findings of phi_overlap_lint.py — the spec entries that currently
name a variable some row's ground-truth phi refines over.
This is a DEBT LIST, not an exemption list. Every entry names the generic
mechanism that removes the need for it; when that mechanism lands, the spec
entry is DELETED and its line here is deleted with it. `accepted debt: 0` is
the deliverable, and it is what makes the claim 'no per-game configuration
references any variable appearing in a ground-truth specification' something
the build checks rather than something the paper asserts.
Adding a line here to make a new entry pass is the exact practice the lint
exists to stop. The only legitimate additions are (a) an entry that predates
the lint, and (b) an entry whose reason is a mechanism, with a plan.
A reason is mandatory and is checked for emptiness, not for content — so the
convention is: name the mechanism, not the row.

accepted.name: bullets_alive
accepted.reason: CONSUMER-SIDE: a count of objects satisfying a predicate is not a member of anything. Retired by a counting quantifier in the atom language, not by any instrumenter change

accepted.name: game_time_ms
accepted.reason: global reporting: g_game_time is file-scope, so it is outside the locals+members universe until namespace-scope variables of scanned TUs are included

accepted.name: m_last_gain_time
accepted.reason: derived scaling: the factor should come from an observation pass over a real trace (--suggest-scaling), not from a hand-named site
prose for the bullets_alive entry; deleted with it
singleton roots: SoundManager becomes a reported object, so its locals need no host route

accepted.name: hurt
accepted.reason: accessor reporting: Player::is_hurt() IS m_post_damage_safety_timer.started(), and Timer publishes fields only, so the composed timer object carries period/cycle_start but not the predicate over them. Retired when the instrumenter reports a closure class's public const nullary accessors alongside its fields — which also retires the rest of this extra_keys block (dying, dead, invincible, swimming, stone, winning, facing) and BadGuy's (active, frozen, in_water). phi then respells to player.post_damage_safety_timer.started == false

HISTORICAL, not a live rule: the paragraph records that four policy.include pins which rescued four benchmark rows were DELETED once GET_META/GET_CHUNK removed the datagram budget that motivated them. Deleting the prose would delete the evidence that the debt was paid. Retired when the paper carries that history instead of the spec

LIVE selection bias, the last one: scan_globs is two files and the prose justifies the choice by how many dataset rows each serves, and names the mutated files it leaves out. The real constraint behind it is real — build_snapshot() drops map-node objects once the snapshot passes gamerv_max_snapshot_bytes, so keys are paid for in nodes. Retired by measuring the widened scan against a real trace's node count, as Super Tux Kart's _scan_globs_comment does for its own globs, and then either widening or justifying the narrowing by the node budget alone

_retired_comment: Debt that HAS been retired, kept for provenance: each line is an entry that
was in `accepted` until the mechanism named in `retired_by` landed and the
spec entry it excused was deleted. The lint does not read this list.
Trajectory: 25 accepted -> 5, over the nested-composition work (member
closure, nested overrides, container members, enum-array elements, singleton
roots, auto-decomposition) plus geometry moving into the snapshot ABI.

_retired.name: x
_retired.retired_by: nested override through MovingObject::m_col -> Rectf (m_p1/m_size are private), plus a one-time `geometry` path declaration in the game's game_profile.json — the consumer's positional bbox reads now resolve a declared path instead of a flat key (game_profile.geometry_path), so geometry no longer has to stay flat
